main_text.p: unius miliaris intervallum, quin imo ad 8. vel 10. stadia duntaxat, e fan-guinis effluit quantilla portione virtu-tem prodire, quae aere ventoque ad-verso non minus, quam secundo, fe-ratur ad vulnus unde sanguis profluxit, ibidemque curationi quomodocunque inservit. Curtria Avium genera, nem-pe Vultures, Anseres, ac Perdices, maxi-me odoris senlu excellant, ita ut etiam Anseribus majorem sagacitatem vimque odorandi quam Canibus tribuerint Ve-terés, rationem reddit Conr. Vit. Schnei-derus de Offe Cribriform. & Senfu ac Or-gano Odoratus, pag. 181. & seqq. ab ipsa hujusce organi structura defumptam. Quod si tamen quis credat non posse odorem realem, seu halitum ipsum, qui odo-rem vehit, a cadaveribus putrescenti-bus, per tam longa locorum spatia deve-ni; intentionalis odorum species, (ut vulgo dicuntur) illi liceat concipere, seu im-presfa quodammodo corpuscul is aereis exhalationum vestigia, five certos in-cunque.

page.notes: Scan is somewhat faint at the right edge. Several words in the first lines are uncertain and have been read against the sense; the original Latin in lines 1-3 reads "unius miliaris intervallum" with "unius" partly obscured. Words with doubtful letters are unmarked where I could not confidently read them; the last line ends mid-word "incunque" and is probably "quaecunque" with an abbreviation mark, which I have left as printed. No engraving, stamps or marginal notes are visible.
